main_text.l: Caput. 9.
NOnum caput vnico argumento, eoque
ab ipsius Pauli libertati suæ in aliorum
gratiam renuntiantis exemplo, sumpto idolol-
atricas illas comessationes hominum saluti
plurimum officientes dissuadet: Nam quod
Paulus in Corinthiorum,
hoc Corinthios in fra-
trum gratiam facere æquum est. Duplicem li-
bertatis suæ renuntiationem proponit, vnam par-
ticularem, qua à debito stipendio ab ecclesijs
exigendo abstinuit. De hac agitur vsq; ad vers.
19. alteram generalem, qua omnes suas actio-
nes, ad hanc non suæ libertatis sed alienæ salu-
tis normam exigit. In reliquo capite in priore
parte duo ostendit, primùm se optimo iure
aliquam & quidem satis amplam laboris sui
mercedem capere potuisse vsque ad vers. 15.
Secundò se hoc non fecisse vers. 15.16.17.18.
ius probatur hoc argumento, Apostolis vtpo-
te primariis euangelij ministris, iustum sti-
pendium exigere licet: At Ego sum Aposto-
lus. Assumptio, quæ priore loco proponi-
tur, in primis verbis occurrit duobus argu-
mentis stabilita: vna à causa efficiente &
formali apostolatus, immediata ipsius Dei vo-
catio

page.notes: The first letter N is a large woodcut initial joined to "Onum". The text continues beyond the bottom of this part. Some words in the first line are printed with spacing irregularities; "Paulus in Corinthiorum" appears to omit a word (the printed text reads as shown). Part 2 of a page; the upper part is cut off. The catchword and signature are as printed; "cationē" is partly obscured. The final word may be "vocatione" with the -ne partly lost; read as "vocatione" in the line "vo-" / "cationes" at the foot.
